text: One of the most iconic sporting venues in Asia for this quarter final fixture between Al Ahli of Saudi Arabia and Buriram United of Thailand. This is the AFC Champions League Elite Finals Jeddah 2025 presented by NEOM.
No room for error on the road to the final, which will take place on the 3rd of May, and the reward for the winner of this fixture will be that semifinal clash on the 29th of April against Al Hilal.
Pretty warm conditions

at this time of the year, slightly cooler now than it was earlier in the day and mercifully, there is a nice bit of breeze blowing across the ground which will help provide some relief. Still 32 degrees Celsius,

something for the players from both sides to have to deal with, along with the fans who have gathered here this evening at this wonderful venue where the journey towards the crown continues at the jewel.
Under the blazing lights of the King Abdullah Sports City Stadium, a battle for supremacy is about to unfold. Al-Ahli, giants of Saudi football armed with world class talent
stand ready to unleash their firepower against the fearless warriors from Thailand Buriram United in your picture right now, being led here by Dion Cools.
They arrive with a burning desire to shock the continent
...and create history.
And looking forward to this challenge, and boy, will it be a challenge this evening.

Welcome along to the continuation of what has been an incredible competition so far, the AFC Champions League Elite 2024-25, which started all the way back in September of last year with 24 teams from the East and West zones, split into two leagues of 12,
and after months of top-level football across this amazing continent of Asia, we are now down to the AFC Champions League Elite Finals Jeddah 2025.
And we're all set to take in this quarterfinal contest between Al Ahli and Buriram United here in the city known for its spirit of hospitality and its love of sport,
a city that welcomes the world, yet fiercely champions its own. And one of its own is in action tonight. Al Ahli will have the backing...
of a fierce home support
as they look to make their way past a Buriram United side who will be keen to silence the crowd
by causing an upset this evening.
This is the second quarter final of the AFC Champions League Elite Finals Jeddah 2025, with the first one taking place last night
between Al Hilal, four time champions, and Gwangju FC, debutants at this level.
There was no upset last night at this ground as Al Hilal dominated and destroyed their opposition on the pitch in a strong display
to send a message to the rest of the contenders at these finals, a 7-0 thrashing of the side from Korea Republic.
An explosive start to these finals, and the question now is what sort of response will we get
from their Saudi Arabian rivals, Al Ahli, and from Southeast Asia's only representatives at this stage of the competition, Buriram United.
Well, here they come, Al Ahli.
Ivan Toney in your picture there.
Just behind him, Merih Demiral sporting a
pretty nice mustache there, bit of a new look for Demiral.
And it's all very friendly.
In the tunnels, it'll all be very friendly in the pre-match handshakes, but that's about where it ends.
Both these teams will be looking to send their own messages of intent tonight.
Al Ahli do come into this match as favorites. They are the only unbeaten side left in this tournament.
Nine wins and a draw from their 10 matches on their journey into this quarter-final.
Five wins from their first five league stage fixtures gave them a perfect start and a solid platform to build on.
As they picked up wins against Persepolis, Al Wasl, Al Rayyan, Al Shorta and Al Ain with three of those games being away matches.
The Iranian side Esteghlal then halted their momentum with a 2-2 draw here at this venue.
They were actually moments away from a big win, but were denied all three points by a late Ivan Toney penalty. That draw proved to be just a minor speed bump for Al Ahli
as they cruised into the round of 16 with back-to-back wins against Qatari clubs Al Sadd who are also at these finals,
they'll be in action tomorrow, and Al Gharafa, with Al Ahli scoring seven goals in those two matches as they wrapped up their league stage fixtures in style.
They would then come up against another Qatari side in the round of 16 with Al Rayyan standing in their way.

They were comfortably brushed aside over two legs with Al Ahli scoring five goals and conceding just once: 3-1 win in the first leg meeting on the road, then sealing their place at these AFC Champions League

league finals back in 2025. With a 2-0 victory in the return match, they now have the advantage of being the home team at these finals, and they'll be looking to make the most of it in their quest for continental glory.
In their way, a stubborn, resilient Buriram United side with the potential to cause an upset.
There will be no fear from a team who have been the dominant force in Thai football for well over a decade.
Giants of Thailand are back in the quarter-finals for the first time since 2013, when they made it out of the group stage on that occasion on goal difference ahead of Jiangsu.

This time around, at the league stage, Buriram started off their campaign without a defeat in their first three matches: 0-0 draw against Vissel Kobe in their opening match, followed by back-to-back wins against Central Coast Mariners and Pohang Steelers.
Things were looking nice and positive for Buriram in the league until matchday four and five, when they suffered consecutive defeats against the two Japanese sides,
who are also featuring in these
ACL Elite Finals 2024-2025. A 5-0 loss to Yokohama F. Marinos
was followed by a 3-0 defeat against Kawasaki Frontale. They bounced back in their final three league stage matches though with draws against Johor Darul Ta'zim and
Gwangju FC combined with an impressive 2-1 win over two-time champions Ulsan HD, enough to see them progressing into the round of 16.
Well, this is what Al-Ahli have gone with for their starting 11 tonight, and it is a strong lineup. They've made three changes
from their last outing in this competition. Edouard Mendy comes back into goal for the side in place of Abdulrahman Al-Sanbi,
Ezgjan Alioski makes his first start of this season's competition as he replaces Matteo Jaimes at left-back. Ziyad Al-Johani gets the nod in central midfield

and he takes the place of Gabri Veiga, who is on the bench this evening, and it's a bench with quality as well. Likes of Firas Al-Buraikan, Sumaihan Al-Nabit, Aleksander Da Costa, and Matteo Jaimes amongst the options if needed.
Sixth match in this season's AFC Champions League Elite for Ahmed Al-Kaf
as the referee. The Omani has plenty in the way of experience, though.
This being his 58th match as a referee at this level of competition.
He'll be assisted by Abubakar Al-Amri, also of Oman, and Jun Mihara of Japan. The fourth official is also from Japan, Yusuke Araki.
VAR for this one will be Muhammad Taqi of Singapore, and the assistant VAR from Qatar, Khamis Al-Marri.
Well, Buriram United have made five changes from their last fixture in this competition against Johor Darul Ta'zim.
They have left quite a few of their regulars on the bench for this one.
There are opportunities for Seksan Ratree, Rattanakorn Maikami and Rene Renner, maybe getting their first start of this season's competition.
Sasalak Haiprakhon also comes into the side along with Marcelo Djaló.
Top scorer Bissoli is left on the bench for this one, and he's joined by the likes of Supachai Chaided, Lucas Crispim, Ken Dougall, and Goran Caušić.
Well, the players gathered in front of their fans, as they usually do.
Customary for them to receive the adulation,
to realize what they are playing for, not just for themselves...
